gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Gugi has lowercase letters that climb almost to the capitals, with terminals cut open so every curve breathes outward. And Noto Sans Armenian, a sans-serif with full, wide-mouthed round letters, gives the display lines a friendlier, more approachable partner.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Gugi's tall lowercase and open-cut terminals look bold, drawn with unshaded, constant strokes. But Noto Sans Avestan, a plain sans with a pronounced x-height and curve tips that never touch, is the one built to carry the quieter text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Noto Sans Balinese has short ascenders and a breathing space inside every curved glyph, so its text looks tidy and modern. Gugi's strokes run contrast-free from stem to terminal, so if the heading shrinks or the body grows, the two lose their separation.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Noto Sans Bamum reads open and modern, with big counters. Gugi draws its letters like fine rope laid down, which gives headings a bold, distinctive look, while the sans body does the quiet work of keeping the text easy going.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Gugi leaves the single-width trail of a rolling-ball pen, with tall lowercase that nearly touches its capitals and open-cut terminals. Its boldness sits well against a plain sans with a dominant midsection.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-batak: Gugi holds a pen line at one width throughout, with tall lowercase and terminals cut open. But Noto Sans Batak, a sans with a towering x-height and a wide-open e, deserves a slightly larger size than the heading suggests.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Bold, tall and round-rimmed, Gugi announces itself at once. Noto Sans Bengali, a sans-serif with capitals barely taller than its lowercase and distinctly open mouths, would carry a long passage smoothly and without any fuss.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Gugi is bold, with tall lowercase and no calligraphic swell on any downstroke. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki, a sans of coiled, swollen letters, looks best a touch larger than the heading's size would suggest.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Tall, bold and open-cut: that is Gugi. Noto Sans Brahmi, a plain sans with a high mean line and open-ended curves, would carry a long passage with a contemporary, unfussy ease.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Gugi is tall, bold and round, with curves that match its stems exactly. Noto Sans Buhid, a sans with generous gaps between curve ends and stems, gives those loud headings a spacious, modern companion beneath.
